name: Kepler-452
tagline: 'Earth 2.0' — a Sun-like star hosting a rocky planet in its habitable zone.
history: Kepler-452b was called 'Earth's older cousin' when announced in 2015 — a roughly 1.6-Earth-radius world circling a near-twin of our Sun every 385 days, comfortably inside the habitable zone where liquid water could pool. The star is ~6 billion years old, so the planet has had longer than Earth to cook up whatever it might hold. Whether it is rocky, gassy or ocean-wrapped stays unknown across 1,800 light-years — it remains one of the closest analogs to home we know.
source: NASA Kepler Mission · NASA Exoplanet Archive
